evidenceProvenance.controller: Razer Synapse AppEngine 4.0.821.53 with OpenBlade capture tooling at 4f2bf1565c7557439760db7e45104bb1e8b62bfd

action.name: Normal Synapse exit and reopening from Auto
action.value: Operator exited Synapse normally from Auto, observed no physical pad change, then reopened Synapse and confirmed Auto and original lighting

validation.applyResult: No OpenBlade device command was performed. The operator confirmed the normal vendor exit and reported no noticed fan, lighting, flashing-red or sleep change.
validation.readbackResult: Application-process absence was confirmed at three separate snapshots; remaining vendor services stayed running. No independent active fan state, target, RPM or ownership readback was obtained.
validation.restorationResult: The operator reopened Synapse normally and confirmed unchanged Auto mode, full-brightness static-green lighting and normal fan behavior.
validation.restorationReadbackResult: Vendor startup transactions and restored application processes were observed separately from operator UI/physical confirmation. The OpenBlade service restarted after graceful capture completion with no reported errors.

sanitizedEvidence.summary: The fixed capture preflight independently checked RZ09-05289EN4 BIOS 2.02 and the exact PID 0F43 revision-0200 pad before selecting only that pad. The saved operator baseline was Auto, full-brightness static-green lighting.

Normal Synapse exit correlated with exactly one 00/04 request carrying 0000 and a matching status-02 semantic echo. This is a pad lifecycle candidate, not an admitted accessory release or a transferred laptop-mode interpretation.

Three separate process snapshots found zero RazerAppEngine instances before reopening. Razer Elevation Service, Razer Game Manager Service 3 and thx_rznb11_service remained running; they were not stopped. No complete Razer control report occurs between the exit acknowledgement and the first startup request.

Vendor startup includes a 00/04 request carrying 0300 and matching status-02 semantic echo. Later two 00/84 queries each return 0300. These raw values are observed pad-mode candidates; their meaning is not borrowed from laptop mode contracts.

Startup contains two acknowledged 0D/10 000600 pairs among other initialization and lighting exchanges. There are no 0D/01 dynamic-demand writes or 0D/81, 0D/88 or 0D/90 fan queries. Two brightness queries return 0105FF and two brightness setters echo 0100FF, consistent with the operator-confirmed full-brightness setting.

The selected capture contains 112 lighting frame requests. The last pre-exit frame and first reopened frame are separated by 137.766635 seconds. The operator saw no physical lighting change while frames were absent. Reopening includes a brief burst of progressively brighter green frame values before steady full-green frames; this encoded ramp was not reported as a visible fade.

All 173 complete 90-byte Razer bodies pass checksum validation. Thirty observed GET_REPORT setup packets use wire selector 0300, interface zero and length 90; this does not establish Windows user-mode report-ID framing. Capture stopped gracefully and the previously running OpenBlade service restarted with no reported errors.

limitations: Normal application exit is not proof that all vendor controllers are absent. Vendor services remained running, and retained device or driver state was not excluded.

Process snapshots sample three points rather than continuous absence. The complete-report silence and lighting-frame gap are separately measured from the raw capture, not extrapolated from process counts.
The 00/04 exit/startup values and 00/84 query responses are pad-specific candidates. No laptop Driver/Normal semantics, safe release, admission or production ownership contract is assigned.
No fan target, active-mode or tachometer getter was observed. Lack of dynamic-demand writes does not prove fan behavior under changing thermal load.
The raw USB report-ID-zero transport remains separate from unvalidated Windows user-mode framing; neither user-mode ID zero nor historical ID 05 is admitted here.
Initialization includes device-identification responses. Serial-bearing payloads and all unrelated identification data are deliberately excluded from this annotation; raw transcripts remain private.
No OpenBlade pad write was performed. The earlier negative standalone 000600 handback result is not superseded by this vendor-controlled lifecycle.
Operator-visible persistence describes this bounded static-green observation only; it does not prove firmware-native effects, arbitrary frame persistence or lighting recovery safety.

productionAdmission.reason: Vendor mode-family transitions are correlated with normal exit and startup, but safe independent OpenBlade handback, meaningful readback and user-mode framing remain unvalidated.

notes: The operator's final preferred state remains Auto with full-brightness static-green lighting. No further pad setting was changed by OpenBlade tooling.
Vendor processes were exited and reopened by the operator through the normal application flow. No vendor process was killed and no vendor service was stopped.
The injected descriptors, raw PCAP, identification replies, process IDs, paths, controller inventories and marker logs remain private and uncommitted.
